method_card.title: How to Interpret Real-Life Graphs
steps: Check the axes first: distance-time or speed-time?
Distance-time: the gradient is the speed; a flat line means stopped.
Speed-time: the gradient is the acceleration; the area underneath is the distance.
Match the units before dividing (turn minutes into hours).
method_card.content:
Distance-time graphs show a journey. The gradient is the speed: steeper means faster, and a flat section means stopped.

Speed-time graphs show how speed changes. The gradient is the acceleration, and the area under the line is the total distance. Split that area into triangles and rectangles.

Always read the axis labels first, and convert minutes to hours before dividing.
method_card.example:
A car travels at 60 km/h for 45 minutes. How far does it go?

45 min = 0.75 h, so distance = 60 × 0.75 = 45 km.

problem_bank.bronze_description: Read distance-time graphs and use speed = distance ÷ time with matching units.
problem_bank.silver_description: Read speed-time graphs: gradient for acceleration, area for distance, plus minute-to-hour conversions.
problem_bank.gold_description: Multi-stage journeys: total distance from combined areas, and average speed over a whole trip.

bronze.display: The distance-time graph shows a jogger's run. How long did the jogger rest for?
bronze.hint: A rest is a flat, horizontal section; measure how long it lasts.

misconceptions.message: A rest is a flat, horizontal line. It runs from 20 min to 40 min, so the rest lasts 40 − 20 = 20 minutes. If you wrote 40 you read the end time, not the length.

guided_steps.say: A rest shows up as a flat, horizontal section: the distance is not changing.

guided_steps.pre: The flat part starts at time =
guided_steps.hint: Read where the line first goes flat.

guided_steps.pre: The flat part ends at time =
guided_steps.hint: Read where the line starts climbing again.
Take the start time from the end time.

guided_steps.pre: Check: over that flat part the distance stayed at
guided_steps.hint: Read the height of the flat line.
guided_steps.done: The distance did not change, so the jogger really rested for 20 minutes.

bronze.display: The distance-time graph shows a cyclist's journey. What was the cyclist's speed during the first 10 minutes? Give your answer in km per minute.
bronze.hint: Read the distance at 10 minutes, then divide it by 10.

misconceptions.message: Speed = distance ÷ time = 4 ÷ 10 = 0.4 km/min. If you got 2.5 you divided time by distance, which is upside down.

guided_steps.say: Speed is distance ÷ time. Read the graph to get the distance first.

guided_steps.pre: Read the distance at time = 10 min:
guided_steps.hint: Follow the line up to t = 10 and read across.

guided_steps.done: It returns the 4 km on the graph, so 0.4 km/min is right.

bronze.display: The distance-time graph shows a person's journey. What total distance did the person travel?
bronze.hint: The total distance is the final height the line reaches.

misconceptions.message: The line never comes back down, so the total distance is its final height at t = 50: 24 km. If you got 18 you stopped reading at t = 40.

guided_steps.say: The line only ever goes up or stays flat, so the total distance is the value it finishes on.

guided_steps.pre: Read the distance at time = 40 min:
guided_steps.hint: Follow the line up to t = 40.

guided_steps.pre: Read the final distance at time = 50 min:
guided_steps.hint: Follow the line to its right-hand end.
The final height is the total distance here.
guided_steps.done: The line does not return toward 0, so 24 km is the whole distance travelled.

bronze.display: A car travels 150 km in 3 hours. What is the average speed?

misconceptions.message: Speed = distance ÷ time = 150 ÷ 3 = 50 km/h. Dividing time by distance (0.02) is upside down.

guided_steps.say: Average speed is total distance ÷ total time.

guided_steps.hint: The distance is given in the question.

guided_steps.done: It returns the 150 km given, so 50 km/h is right.

bronze.display: A bus travels at 40 km/h for 2 hours. How far does it go?

misconceptions.message: Distance = speed × time = 40 × 2 = 80 km. If you got 20 you divided; here you multiply speed by time.

guided_steps.hint: The speed is given in the question.
Two hours at 40 km each hour.

guided_steps.done: It returns the 40 km/h given, so 80 km is right.

bronze.display: A train covers 240 km at 80 km/h. How many hours does it take?

misconceptions.message: Time = distance ÷ speed = 240 ÷ 80 = 3 hours. Multiplying (19200) instead of dividing is the slip.

guided_steps.hint: The distance is given in the question.
How many 80 km chunks fit into 240 km.

guided_steps.done: It returns the 240 km given, so 3 hours is right.

bronze.display: On a distance-time graph, what does a horizontal line represent?
bronze.hint: On a distance-time graph, flat means not moving.

misconceptions.message: On a distance-time graph, horizontal means stopped. On a speed-time graph, horizontal means constant speed. Do not mix them up.

bronze.display: On a speed-time graph, what does the area under the line represent?
bronze.hint: The area under a speed-time graph gives distance.

misconceptions.message: Area under a speed-time graph = distance travelled. The gradient (not the area) gives acceleration.

silver.display: The speed-time graph shows a car's journey. What is the acceleration during the first 10 seconds?
silver.hint: Acceleration is the gradient: change in speed ÷ time.

misconceptions.message: Acceleration = change in speed ÷ time = 20 ÷ 10 = 2 m/s². If you got 0.5 you divided time by the speed change.

guided_steps.say: Acceleration is the gradient of a speed-time graph: change in speed ÷ time.

guided_steps.pre: Read the speed at time = 10 s:
guided_steps.hint: Follow the line up to t = 10.
Share the speed gain over 10 seconds.

guided_steps.pre: Check: 2 m/s² for 10 s gives a speed gain of 2 × 10 =
guided_steps.done: It matches the 20 m/s on the graph, so 2 m/s² is right.

silver.display: Using the same speed-time graph, find the total distance travelled in 20 seconds.
silver.hint: Split the area into a triangle then a rectangle and add them.

misconceptions.message: Split the area: triangle (0 to 10 s) ½ × 10 × 20 = 100, plus rectangle (10 to 20 s) 10 × 20 = 200, total 300 m. Treating it all as one rectangle gives 400, too big.

guided_steps.say: Distance is the area under the line. Split it into a triangle then a rectangle.

guided_steps.hint: Divide distance by total time to sanity-check.
guided_steps.done: 15 m/s sits between 0 and 20, so 300 m is sensible.

silver.display: A car travels at 60 km/h for 45 minutes. How far does it go?
silver.hint: Turn 45 minutes into 0.75 hours first, then multiply.

misconceptions.message: Convert 45 min to 0.75 h first, then 60 × 0.75 = 45 km. Using 45 as if it were hours gives 2700 km.

guided_steps.say: The speed is in km/h, so the time must be in hours first.

guided_steps.hint: There are 60 minutes in an hour.
Multiply the speed by the time in hours.

guided_steps.done: It returns the 60 km/h given, so 45 km is right.

silver.display: A cyclist travels 18 km in 45 minutes. What is the speed in km/h?
silver.hint: Turn 45 minutes into 0.75 hours, then divide distance by it.

misconceptions.message: Change 45 min to 0.75 h, then 18 ÷ 0.75 = 24 km/h. Dividing by 45 gives 0.4, which is km per minute, not km/h.

guided_steps.say: For km/h the time must be in hours first.

guided_steps.hint: There are 60 minutes in an hour.
Divide the distance by the time in hours.

guided_steps.done: It returns the 18 km given, so 24 km/h is right.

silver.display: The speed-time graph shows a car that decelerates from 30 m/s to 0 in 6 seconds. What is the deceleration?
silver.hint: Deceleration is change in speed ÷ time; give it as a positive value.

misconceptions.message: Deceleration = change in speed ÷ time = 30 ÷ 6 = 5 m/s². Dividing time by the speed change (0.2) is upside down.

guided_steps.say: Deceleration is the size of the gradient: how fast the speed drops.

guided_steps.pre: Check: losing 5 m/s each second for 6 s loses 5 × 6 =
guided_steps.done: That is the full 30 m/s, from 30 down to 0, so 5 m/s² is right.

silver.display: The speed-time graph shows a constant speed of 15 m/s for 8 seconds. What distance is covered?
silver.hint: A flat speed-time line gives a rectangle: base × height.

misconceptions.message: The speed is constant, so the area is a rectangle: 8 × 15 = 120 m. Using ½ (as for a triangle) gives 60, which is wrong for a flat line.

guided_steps.say: The line is flat, so the area under it is a rectangle.

guided_steps.done: It returns the constant 15 m/s, so 120 m is right.

silver.display: The speed-time graph shows a car accelerating from 0 to 24 m/s in 8 seconds. Find the distance using the area under the graph.
silver.hint: The area of the triangle is ½ × base × height.

misconceptions.message: Area of the triangle = ½ × 8 × 24 = 96 m. Leaving out the ½ gives 192, the rectangle by mistake.

guided_steps.say: The line is a straight slope from 0, so the area under it is a triangle.

guided_steps.pre: The base is 8 s and the height is
guided_steps.hint: The height is the top speed reached.
Average speed times time gives distance.
guided_steps.done: Both methods give 96 m, so the answer is right.

gold.display: The speed-time graph shows a car. It accelerates from 0 to 25 m/s in 10 s, then travels at 25 m/s for 20 s, then decelerates to 0 in 5 s. Find the total distance.
gold.hint: Split into triangle, rectangle, triangle and add the three areas.

misconceptions.message: Triangle + rectangle + triangle = ½(10)(25) + 20(25) + ½(5)(25) = 125 + 500 + 62.5 = 687.5 m. Forgetting the ½ on the sloped parts gives 875.

guided_steps.say: The shape is a trapezium: two sloped triangles either side of a rectangle.

guided_steps.hint: base × height for the 20 s at 25 m/s.

guided_steps.done: 687.5 m over 35 s averages about 19.6 m/s, between 0 and 25, so it is sensible.

gold.display: A runner completes a 400 m lap. The first 200 m takes 25 s, and the second 200 m takes 35 s. What is the average speed for the whole lap? Give your answer to 1 d.p.
gold.hint: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time, not the mean of the speeds.

misconceptions.message: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 400 ÷ 60 = 6.7 m/s. Averaging the two speeds (8 and about 5.7) gives about 6.9, which is wrong.

guided_steps.say: Average speed always uses the totals, never the mean of the two separate speeds.

guided_steps.hint: Divide total distance by total time, to 1 d.p.

guided_steps.pre: Check: the mean of 8 and 5.7 would be about 6.9, but total ÷ total gives
guided_steps.done: Average speed is total distance over total time, so 6.7 m/s is right.

gold.display: A train accelerates uniformly from rest to 30 m/s in 12 seconds. Find the acceleration.

misconceptions.message: Acceleration = change in speed ÷ time = 30 ÷ 12 = 2.5 m/s². Dividing time by the speed change (0.4) is upside down.

guided_steps.say: Acceleration is change in speed ÷ time. From rest means the start speed is 0.

guided_steps.done: It reaches the 30 m/s given, so 2.5 m/s² is right.

gold.display: The speed-time graph shows a trapezium: speed rises from 0 to 20 m/s in 4 s, stays at 20 m/s for 6 s, then drops to 0 in 2 s. Find the total distance.
gold.hint: Add the two triangle areas and the rectangle area.

misconceptions.message: ½(4)(20) + 6(20) + ½(2)(20) = 40 + 120 + 20 = 180 m. Forgetting the ½ on the sloped parts gives 240.

guided_steps.say: The trapezium splits into two triangles and a rectangle.

guided_steps.hint: base × height for the 6 s at 20 m/s.

guided_steps.done: 180 m over 12 s averages 15 m/s, between 0 and 20, so it is sensible.

gold.display: Two cyclists start together. Cyclist A travels at 12 km/h. Cyclist B travels at 16 km/h. After 3 hours, how far apart are they?
gold.hint: Find each distance, then subtract, or use the speed difference × time.

misconceptions.message: Gap = (16 − 12) × 3 = 12 km. Adding the two distances (36 + 48 = 84) answers a different question.

guided_steps.say: They travel the same way, so the gap is the difference in how far each goes.

guided_steps.hint: Subtract the smaller distance from the larger.

guided_steps.pre: Check: the speed gap is 16 − 12 = 4 km/h, and over 3 h that is 4 × 3 =
guided_steps.hint: The gap grows by the speed difference each hour.
guided_steps.done: Both methods give 12 km, so the answer is right.

steps.label: Distance
steps.content: Area under graph = ½ × base × height = ½ × 10 × 20 = 100 m

worked_examples.question: A car accelerates from 0 to 20 m/s in 10 seconds. Find the acceleration and distance travelled.

bronze.title: Bronze: speed, distance and time
steps: Speed = distance ÷ time. Rearranged: distance = speed × time, and time = distance ÷ speed.
On a distance-time graph, a flat line means stopped and a steeper line means faster.
Keep units matched: km with hours gives km/h.

example.question: A car travels 180 km in 4 hours. Find its speed.

silver.title: Silver: speed-time graphs and unit changes
steps: On a speed-time graph the gradient is the acceleration: change in speed ÷ time.
The area under a speed-time graph is the distance. Split it into triangles and rectangles.
Change minutes to hours before dividing: 45 min = 45 ÷ 60 = 0.75 h.

example.question: A car speeds up from 0 to 20 m/s in 8 s. Find the acceleration.

gold.title: Gold: multi-stage journeys
steps: Break a journey into stages: speeding up, steady, slowing down. Work out each stage on its own.
For total distance, add the area of every stage: two triangles and a rectangle for a trapezium.
For average speed use total distance ÷ total time, never the mean of the separate speeds.

example.question: A bus goes from 0 to 15 m/s in 5 s, then holds 15 m/s for 10 s. Total distance?

opener.display: The graph shows Sam's bike ride to the park and back. Distance from home is on the up axis, time in minutes along the bottom.

steps.pre: How far away is the park? Read the highest the line reaches:
steps.hint: The line climbs, then flattens. Read that flat height.

steps.pre: Sam waited at the park while the line is flat, from 15 min to 30 min. How many minutes is that?
steps.hint: Take the start time from the end time of the flat part: 30 − 15.

steps.pre: The whole trip finishes where the line reaches 0 again. At what time, in minutes?
steps.hint: Read the time where the line touches the bottom on the right.

steps.say: You just read a distance-time graph by common sense. The height is distance from home, a flat line means not moving, and a steeper slope means going faster. That slope is the speed. Speed-time graphs work the same way, and their area gives distance. That is the whole of today's lesson.

bronze.display: A coach drives 120 km in 3 hours at a steady speed, then keeps going for 2 more hours at the same speed. How far does it travel in total?

steps.say: Steady speed means we can find one speed and reuse it for the rest of the trip.

steps.hint: Divide the distance by the time.

steps.pre: At that speed each hour covers
steps.hint: At 40 km/h you go 40 km every hour.
Add the first part to the extra part.
steps.done: Same speed throughout, so the distances just add up. That was the whole point.

silver.display: The speed-time graph shows a motorbike. It speeds up from rest to 18 m/s in 6 s, then holds 18 m/s until 14 s. Find the total distance.

steps.say: On a speed-time graph the area under the line is the distance. Split it into a triangle and a rectangle.

steps.hint: Gradient is change in speed over time.
Area of a triangle is ½ × base × height.
The steady part lasts from 6 s to 14 s, that is 8 s.

steps.done: Area under the graph is the distance. That was the whole point.

gold.display: A tram speeds up from rest to 12 m/s in 4 s, holds 12 m/s for 10 s, then slows to rest in 3 s. Find the total distance.

steps.say: A trapezium splits into two triangles and a rectangle. Find each area, then add.

steps.hint: base × height, over the 10 s at 12 m/s.

steps.done: Every stage's area adds to the total distance. That was the whole point.
